chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Wuheyb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the death of the believer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer dies with every death; he dies by drowning, and he dies by crushing, and is afflicted by beasts, and he dies by the thunderbolt, and the thunderbolt does not strike the one who remembers Allah, Exalted and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: Does a believer die from the same causes as others, and what is the specific protection against the thunderbolt?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while believers are subject to natural causes of death like drowning or being crushed, they are specifically protected from the sudden, fatal strike of the thunderbolt (ṣāʿiqah) if they are among the constant rememberers of Allah (dhākirū Allāh). This distinction highlights the unique spiritual safeguard granted to those who maintain persistent dhikr, distinguishing their fate from the general populace in the context of divine retribution or sudden death. The narration underscores the protective power of mindfulness of God, a core tenet in Shia piety, linking physical safety to spiritual vigilance.
